summary: A is closer to the contract because it confines replayability to the new upload path and preserves the lower-level Add and shared retry behavior. Neither patch is merge-ready: both bypass FilesService.Add, while A also adds expressly forbidden association APIs.
reasons: A leaves FilesService.Add and RawClient retry semantics intact; B changes every io.Reader request by buffering it, directly violating the requirements to preserve Add behavior and avoid unrelated retry refactoring.

A’s retry test uses an *os.File source and verifies byte-identical multipart bodies across attempts, giving stronger coverage of streamed-content replay than B’s Upload retry test with strings.Reader.
Both implementations duplicate Add’s request, decoding, and error path instead of routing the multipart body through Add as required.
B’s global replayableReader changes memory usage, source-read timing, and streaming behavior throughout the SDK, including Files.Update and unrelated RawClient callers.
risks_a: Adds six public association options and multipart form-field machinery despite the explicit prohibition on association fields and FilesOption changes.
Upload calls NewFileWithFields and Raw.Do directly rather than reusing multipartbody.NewFile and FilesService.Add.
The new association option comments mention Add, but Add ignores the added form fields.
risks_b: Globally buffers opaque io.Reader bodies unless WithNoRetry is set, an out-of-scope and potentially high-memory semantic change.
Changes existing Files.Add and Files.Update behavior despite the preservation requirement.
Upload bypasses FilesService.Add, duplicating its option, request, decoding, and error handling path.
